title: Staff member signed in from Portugal an hour after signing in from London

verdict.executive_summary: The alert shows Sofia Novak signing in at 08:19 from London and again at 09:26 from Lisbon, 67 minutes apart, which matches an impossible-travel pattern. Both sign-ins used her usual managed laptop NB-OPS-052 and both passed MFA on her registered phone, with no suspicious follow-on activity. A benign explanation exists because the Lisbon IP is on a mobile network consistent with roaming, but travel or roaming authorisation for this user cannot be confirmed from available sources, so Tier 1 cannot close it under the playbook.
verdict.rationale: This alert type has a matching playbook entry and the required checks were performed. The evidence supports a plausible benign scenario: the same known managed device was used for both sign-ins, MFA was satisfied on the user's registered phone, the Lisbon IP belongs to a mobile carrier consistent with roaming, the user is standard privilege, the host is low criticality, and there was no suspicious activity in either session. However, the playbook allows closure only if a VPN, proxy or corporate roaming explanation explains the location and the device is known managed, in addition to the general close rules. Here, the device condition is met, but the infrastructure explanation is only plausible, not confirmed: there is no record of travel, roaming enablement, or other organisational data proving the user was legitimately abroad at that time. The deciding fact is whether Sofia Novak was physically travelling in Portugal or otherwise legitimately using mobile roaming at 09:26Z. That fact was not obtained from available tooling, so the alert cannot be closed and should be held pending user or manager confirmation rather than escalated immediately, because there is no sign of impact or malicious follow-on activity.
verdict.claim_restated: The rule claims Sofia Novak authenticated from two locations too far apart to travel between in the time available.

verdict.innocent_explanation: Sofia Novak was legitimately travelling and signed in from her normal managed laptop while roaming on a Portuguese mobile network; this fits the evidence that both sign-ins came from her usual device, both were approved with her registered MFA phone, the Lisbon IP belongs to a mobile carrier, and there was no suspicious activity after either sign-in.
verdict.malicious_explanation: An attacker obtained Sofia Novak's password and successfully completed MFA, then accessed the account from Portugal while the legitimate user had recently signed in from London; this would be supported by confirmed user denial of travel, evidence of MFA fatigue or compromise, session anomalies, or suspicious follow-on actions from the Lisbon session.
verdict.deciding_fact: Whether Sofia Novak was legitimately in Portugal or otherwise expected to be using mobile roaming at the time of the 09:26Z sign-in.
verdict.hold_waiting_for: Confirmation from the user or her manager/system owner whether she was travelling in Portugal or legitimately using mobile roaming at 2026-08-29T09:26:00Z.

verdict.containment_considered: No containment was initiated.
